description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

Khyber Pass guns are unlicensed handmade copies of AK-47s, M16s, and Lee-Enfields built in the mountain region between Afghanistan and Pakistan. Local Khyber Pass gunsmiths don't just copy famous firearms — they combine parts from completely different weapons into one gun. One bolt-action AK-47 example uses a Bren gun magazine, a P14 Enfield bolt, and AK-47 body parts all in a single rifle. Other combinations include a Soviet SKS merged with a German G3, and an AK mixed with an HK53 and Czech VZ-58 parts. These are some of the strangest combination firearms ever handmade. Discover the full story of Khyber Pass frankenguns.
